characterList.description: A male with a light complexion and visible wrinkles. He is wearing a light blue, long-sleeved shirt.
characterList.name: Narrator

content_metadata.description: An educational video demonstrating the use of Fourier transform to analyze signals from a touch-tone telephone.

qAndA.question: What is the sampling rate used in the "comedirecord" program?

qAndA.answer: The phone is connected to a USB sound card using a simple circuit with a 10k resistor. (explained and drawn in Scene 1)
qAndA.question: How is the phone connected to the computer?

qAndA.answer: FFTW3 is used to calculate the Fourier Transform, enabling the visualization of the frequency spectrum of the audio signal. (explained in Scene 2)
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of the FFTW3 library?

qAndA.answer: The spectrum displays a complex pattern with numerous frequencies due to the wide range of frequencies present in human speech. (observed in Scene 2)
qAndA.question: What happens to the Fourier Transform spectrum when the narrator speaks into the phone?

qAndA.answer: Touch-tone phones use a dual-tone multi-frequency (DTMF) system, meaning each button generates two specific frequencies simultaneously. (explained in Scene 1 and demonstrated in Scene 2)
qAndA.question: Why does pressing the "0" button produce two distinct peaks in the Fourier Transform spectrum?
